newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland complains to Russia on truck delays.
newsitem.headline: Finland complains to Russia on truck delays.

text.p: Finnish Transport Minister Tuula Linnainmaa has appealed to her Russian counterpart to curb bureaucracy which is making Finnish cargo transport to and from Russia virtually impossible, the ministry said on Friday.

Since the start of the year, Finnish truckers with oversized lorries -- needed for key goods such as wood and food -- have not been able to get permits quickly. Transport of these items has almost come to a halt, a ministry official told Reuters.
Russian authorities require original permits issued only in Moscow, but courier delivery takes two weeks.
"Nobody can wait that long," said director Harri Caven at the transport ministry. "This is a big delay causing losses in trade and traffic."
The transport ministry said in a statement that wood transport from the Vyborg area in the southeast had been completely halted for a couple of weeks.
Caven also said the permissioning system favoured Russian trucks which seemed to be moving normally.
The transport ministry statement said the minister had also asked the Finnish ministry of foreign affairs to issue an official note on the problem.
